top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu alone) is my choice on the common criteria. On public knowledge of the Blinding (Orbitor) trilogy and Solenoid, his is a voice I find nowhere else: memory, the body, dream and cosmological speculation are joined in recursive, densely patterned prose, sustained at large scale over decades. The citation is best anchored in the major prose, with the poetry named as its lyric root, because translated coverage of the poetry and early work is uneven. The open points remain whether Solenoid reworks the Blinding materials or only restages them, and how much of the Romanian patterning, wordplay and rhythm survives in translation. I have not read the originals or independently verified any text, so these are judgments from public knowledge and translation, and a Romanian-language assessment would be the right check. The unanimous opening and round-2 convergence is not literary evidence and I give it no weight. The attribution is clean (one writer, one language). P000 ranks below it because the reservations raised are ones to test, and none has produced a rival with a clearly stronger case or shown the work to fall short of the standard for an award.
recusal_note: none apparent from the profile; my own work as a novelist and critic of historical and psychological fiction is context, not a documented tie to Cărtărescu
